subject: Follow-up: privacy sprint — TTLs for generated content & residency
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@clinix.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo summary + two quick asks on data handling

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — appreciate the walkthrough of your ingestion flow. Short recap and the two things we said we'd follow up on so you can share with security/compliance: 

1) What we store from model runs: by default our hosted runtime persists (a) request metadata (timestamp, model variant, region, and request id) and (b) generation artifacts (text outputs and any user-supplied prompt content) for debugging/quality for a configurable retention window. We do NOT persist KV cache contents as an indexable store beyond the request.

2) Retention / TTL options: we support per-customer retention policies. Common patterns: ephemeral mode (TTL = 0 — outputs and prompts discarded immediately after response), short-term debug (TTL = 30 days), and audit retention (TTL = 13 months). We can map Clinix workloads to a short TTL for production-inference and longer TTL for training/eval if you opt in.

Actions from our side: 
- I’ll attach a one-page summary of the retention controls and the governance checklist Marissa runs with Enterprise for SOC2 evidence.
- Naomi will confirm where logs/telemetry reside (region and access controls) and provide the auth/audit process for on-demand exports.

Two questions for you: 
A) Which of your environments must have EU residency? (prod/dev/etl)
B) For PII in prompts — are you comfortable with short-term TTL (30 days) for dev and ephemeral in prod, or do you need no-storage in all environments?

Next steps: we propose a short privacy sprint (30–45 min) with your SecOps and Data Governance folks to lock TTLs and residency. What time works tomorrow?

—
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_privacy-summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Moreno <alex@clinix.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lin <samantha.lin@clinix.io>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo summary + two quick asks on data handling

Thanks Logan — this is helpful. Quick answers in-line below and a couple follow-ups: 

A) Residency: prod must stay in us-east-1. Dev and ETL can live in us-west-2 for now. We may need EU later for customers in EMEA, but not for the POC.

B) PII in prompts: our security policy says any PHI/PII must not be retained unless explicitly approved for analytics. For the POC, can you confirm there is a mode where generated outputs are returned to the caller but not persisted (no logs that include the prompt or output)? We’d like an assurance for the POC that there is a no-storage mode (TTL=0) for endpoints tagged as "sensitive".

Also, Samantha asked whether you can supply a short mapping of common sensitive fields (SSN, MRN, full name, DOB) and where those show up in tracing/logging so we can audit easily. Can you attach that?

Thanks — Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Product, Clinix Health
alex@clinix.io

On Mon, Nov 22, 2026 at 09:18 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the call this morning — appreciate the walkthrough of your ingestion flow....

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo summary + two quick asks on data handling

Looping in a couple of running notes for the privacy sprint and what we can ship quickly: 
- We have a documented endpoint flag (sensitive=true) that sets ephemeral mode: request body and response text are dropped from our long-term store and are only kept in-memory for the duration of processing. We can enable that per-route.
- Audit logs still capture metadata (request id, timestamp, model version, route id) but we redact prompt and output fields in the retained audit record when ephemeral mode is on. That redaction meets the "no-storage" ask for the POC.
- For customers who need tenant-level residency, we provision dedicated routing so traffic stays in the requested region and logs are stored in the corresponding S3 bucket with enforced KMS and retention policies.

Marissa — I attached the sensitive-fields mapping you asked for and a short checklist for the privacy sprint. For the sprint, I recommend the following invite: Alex, Samantha, Clinix SecOps, Logan, Naomi, Marissa, and one engineer to review endpoint flags. 30–45 minutes should be enough.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: clinix_data_map.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@clinix.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Samantha Lin <samantha.lin@clinix.io>
Date: 2026-11-22T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo summary + two quick asks on data handling

Alex — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Confirming items for the POC / next steps: 
- We will enable ephemeral mode (TTL=0) for any route you tag as "sensitive" — no prompt or output text will be written to long-term storage. Audit records will keep request ids only (redacted prompt/output).
- Prod residency: we will pin your prod routes to us-east-1. Dev/ETL will remain in us-west-2.
- Naomi to provide the short-form evidence pack (S3 bucket names, KMS key IDs, and the redaction proof) prior to the sprint.
- Proposed sprint: tomorrow 10:00am PT. Please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: 1) endpoint flags/demos (10 min) 2) logs & access model (10 min) 3) retention policy & sign-off (10–15 min).

If that works I’ll send the invite and include the relevant Zoom link + the two attachments we referenced.

—
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
